claims.text: As-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts have a homogeneously mixed surface composition.
Holding the catalyst at 0.3 V vs. RHE for 30 minutes in an ethanol-containing electrolyte induces Pt surface enrichment.
The treatment-induced Pt surface enrichment is modest.
The treatment-induced Pt surface enrichment is stable.
The potential hold preferentially decreases the stability of less noble constituent metals.
Preferential leaching of less noble metals such as Rh and Ru can produce the proposed Pt enrichment.
Redistribution of less noble metals can produce the proposed Pt enrichment.
The treatment forms localized Pt-rich surface domains and changes the surface metal distribution.
The modified surface composition changes the adsorption energies or local adsorption properties of ethanol and key reaction intermediates.
Changes in adsorption properties caused by Pt-rich regions steer ethanol oxidation toward acetic acid production.
The Pt-rich surface favors acetic acid formation over complete oxidation to CO2.
Treated catalysts will exhibit greater surface Pt enrichment than untreated catalysts.
Treated catalysts will exhibit higher acetic-acid selectivity than untreated catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
The proposed comparison uses untreated PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts tested under otherwise identical ethanol-oxidation conditions as the baseline.
The proposed hypothesis is limited to room-temperature operation, a 30-minute hold at 0.3 V vs. RHE, and conditions without extensive dissolution or aggregation.
